title: The Future of Domestic Financing for Health is Now: Africa’s Pathway to Sustainable Health Systems
host: The Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage, Republic of Côte d’Ivoire, The Ministry of Health, Republic of South Africa, in collaboration with Global Fund
description: This event is organized by the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, under the leadership of Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, and co-hosted with the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, the African Union Commission (AUC), several regional partners, and the Global Fund.  It will bring together Ministers of Health and Finance, senior national policymakers, global and regional advocates for health financing, and development and donor partners. The objective is to foster dialogue on financial sustainability and the transition of African health sectors from donor dependency to increased domestic financing. It will also offer a platform for countries to share lessons, evidence-informed approaches, and strategies for maintaining essential health services and programs amid fiscal and geopolitical uncertainty.

title: Webinar on the Global Fund, Digital Health and Human Rights
host: Developed Country NGO, Developing Country NGO and Communities Delegations
description:
The Global Fund spends over US$150 million annually to strengthen health information systems, improve the availability and quality of digital data, and provide digital tools for health workers, which leverages private sector partnerships to support its investments. The Developed Country NGO Delegation to the Global Fund Board commissioned a study to investigate the challenges that Global Fund communities and civil society experience in the digital health transformation, viewed from a rights-based perspective. The webinar will present recommendations based on the study, and we will hear from the Global Fund Secretariat and representatives from communities and civil society on how to move these issues forward. Please find the study and brief here.

We invite you to also sign on to this letter to the new Global Fund Committee Leadership to address the recommendations, including the development of a digital strategy under the joint mandate of the Strategy Committee and Audit and Finance Committee, at the upcoming Committee meetings in July.

title: Accélérer et Intensifier le Dépistage de la TB en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre

Lors de la deuxième session, nous nous pencherons sur le positionnement optimal des moyens de diagnostic de la tuberculose au sein des réseaux nationaux de dépistage afin d’atteindre un plus grand nombre de personnes. Nos experts discuteront de la meilleure façon de placer et de distribuer les outils de dépistage de la tuberculose, en tenant compte de leurs caractéristiques, des besoins du système de santé et des préférences des communautés.

title: Health Architecture Reimagined - Civil Society Organisations (HEAR CSO) Launch
host: WACI Health, UHC2030 CSEM, STOPAIDS, NCD Alliance, GFAN, GNP+, ITPC
description:
Developed in response to the impact of the current geopolitical and development finance crisis, and at a moment of unprecedented change, the HEAR CSO Consortium is coordinated by a diverse consortium of civil society and community networks and organisations including WACI Health, UHC2030 CSEM, STOPAIDS, NCD Alliance, GFAN, GNP+ and ITPC. We hope you will join us!

As last weeks UN General Assembly made clear, there is an urgent need to reimagine global health architecture to secure equitable, affordable and effective health care for all. HEAR CSO will create spaces for gathering and amplifying the voices of civil society and community leadership working across health issues and aspects of global health architecture, by which we mean the systems, structures, institutions, rules and processes that collectively guide, coordinate, finance and implement efforts to improve health on a global scale.

title: Follow-Up Webinar on Community Engagement in USG Global Health and Countries MoU Negotiations
host: COMPASS, EANNASO, KP-TNC, Health Gap, Data Etc
description:
On 10th November 2025 a webinar was organized to provide civil society organizations, community advocates, and national stakeholders with a, deep-dive analysis of the draft USG MoUs and Companion Guide, highlighting three critical areas for urgent, country-level advocacy and amendment before the agreements are signed by mid-December. CSOs were also provided with negotiation tools and techniques to ensure the final MoUs are aligned with global targets, responsive to community needs, and focused on genuine public health impact, not just bilateral interests.

Initial intel within countries shows that negotiations are centered in Ministries of Finance, with limited participation from Ministries of Health and almost none from decentralized sub-national units, despite devolved governance in many countries. Senior USG officials are holding brief, highly selective meetings, leaving civil society and community networks outside the room. There is growing indication that USG may favor centralized national-treasury models, which could sideline local government delivery systems that have driven HIV gains. With MoUs expected to be finalized by 12 December 2025, the window for influence is becoming extremely narrow.

Following the 10 November 2025 webinar, participants requested a practical, country-focused follow-up session to share real-time intelligence across MoU countries and collectively strategize ways for communities to engage, even under highly constrained access.

title: Keeping Harm Reduction Alive: Strategies Amid a Global Funding Collapse
description:
Harm Reduction has been long underfunded. Harm Reduction International’s most recent findings show that harm reduction funding is meeting only 6% of the estimated necessary need in low- and middle-income countries. This research came before the United States pulled Official Development Assistance (ODA) funding through projects like PEPFAR, USAID, or pledges to the Global Fund. The situation we now face is undoubtedly more stark, with numerous low- and middle- income countries having been heavily reliant on US funding for harm reduction. Before this year, domestic funding for harm reduction had been decreasing, resulting in over-reliance on bilateral donations or international multilateral donors to fill the gap.

UNAIDS estimates that the permanent discontinuation of this important source of HIV funding will lead to an additional 6.6 million new HIV infections and 4.2 million AIDS-related deaths between 2025 and 2029. Amid this funding crisis we must re-assess our priorities and focus our efforts to retain vital and life-saving harm reduction services. The World Health Organization, along with The Global Fund, has stressed the importance of maintaining and sustaining the continuity of life-saving harm reduction interventions that are under threat. While the guidance is clear about the importance of maintaining these services for sustaining the life and health of people who use drugs - what does it mean for civil society advocacy?

The 2025 Update to the Global State of Harm Reduction allows us to take stock of major changes to harm reduction programming at the national level, providing general insights between editions of the more comprehensive biennial Global State. In the current context – the 2025 Update takes stock of the impact of these US funding cuts, giving us an initial overview of the countries most harshly hit, while highlighting the mitigating factors protecting other countries, such as in those with existing domestic funding for harm reduction

In this context, our work together and the arenas where we could collaborate were fundamental to us and to our mission. We want to express our deep gratitude and our joy to be partners in advancing human rights, gender equality and the meaningful participation of women and girls in their diversity at the center of HIV, TB and malaria responses.

Amid shifting global dynamics, the 8th Replenishment process, and GC7 reprioritization, our collective work has been critical to safeguarding a Global Fund partnership to remain transformative, community & women led. The progress we have made together reflects a shared commitment that we must continue to protect and strengthen in the years ahead.

We are pleased to invite you to the Women4GlobalFund 2025 Highlights of the Year Webinar, where we will:

Share key achievements and milestones from 2025

Les décideurs politiques, les défenseurs de la santé publique et les praticiens ont appelé à une meilleure intégration des agents de santé communautaire (ASC) dans le système de santé en général et dans les soins de sant primaires en particulier. L'appel à l'action de Bangkok encourage les parties prenantes à soutenir l'intégration des soins de santé communautaires professionnels dans les systèmes de santé nationaux en tant que pratique standard, à garantir un soutien à long terme, à utiliser des technologies adaptée et à instaurer la confiance et l'inclusion dans les environnements fragiles afin de protéger les communautés et d'améliorer les résultats en matière de santé.
Dans ce webinaire, nous explorerons les conditions qui permettent la mise en place de mécanismes d'achat stratégique durables pour soutenir l'institutionnalisation des programmes d'ASC et la mise en œuvre de ces programmes, ainsi que les options possibles à cette fin. Les présentations des pays et la table ronde qui suivra porteront sur les expériences du Kenya et du Burkina Faso. Nous entendrons également le témoignage d'une défenseuse des agents de santé communautaire du Kenya.
La session se déroulera en anglais et sera interprétée simultanément en français. Elle sera interactive : vous pourrez poser vos questions aux panélistes.
Au plaisir de partager cette session avec vous!

title: What Could Go Right? Partnering with Communities and Civil Society for New TB Vaccines
description:
New tuberculosis (TB) vaccines could be realized as soon as 2028 — radically reshaping the journey to eliminate TB. Communities and civil society organizations are poised to play a vital role in the introduction of a future TB vaccine as central protagonists of this next chapter for TB elimination.

TAG’s forthcoming report, What Could Go Right? Vital Partnerships with Communities and Civil Society for New Tuberculosis Vaccines, explores the foundational role that community and civil society groups can play in the successful introduction of a new TB vaccine and strategies for capacitating and empowering communities towards that goal. In bringing together three unique sub-studies, this first-of-its-kind report examines community and civil society’s readiness to engage in TB vaccine advocacy and policymaking at national, regional, and global levels, and underscores the transformative role communities can play in TB vaccine introduction, as well as the critical need for other stakeholders to help them realize that potential.

Please join us to discuss What Could Go Right? Partnering with Communities and Civil Society for New TB Vaccine and the path forward to capacitating and engaging community and civil society in the preparation for and introduction of a future TB vaccine.

Development assistance is declining sharply, disease burdens are rising, and outbreaks have increased by over 40% in recent years. This moment demands a clear, Africa-led agenda for Africa's health future.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) Africa, WACI Health, Africa REACH, and partners invite you to a CSO-led webinar on African leadership for health sovereignty.

The session will result in a Civil Society Call to Action urging AU Member States to integrate health sovereignty, sustainable financing, and regional manufacturing into national and regional preparedness plans.

title: The green line: civil society demands for TB vaccine preparedness and access
description:

This includes a growing body of work from the WHO TB Vaccine Accelerator Council and its working group on Financing and Access. Meanwhile, the candidates in late-stage development will require additional resources to bring them to licensure and prepare them for scaled-up rollout. Meaningful civil society and community engagement will be critical to this effort, including to generate demand and hold decision makers accountable.

Join the TB Vaccine Advocacy Roadmap (TB Vax ARM) webinar on Wednesday 11 March to begin a conversation exploring the factors that will shape access to new TB vaccines. Together, we’re working to define common civil society priorities — “green lines” — for access conditions in TB vaccine agreements to inform work by groups such as the TB Vaccine Accelerator Council’s Finance and Access Working Group.

title: What You Need to Know About GC8
description:
The Global Fund has released guidance materials to support applicants preparing funding requests for Grant Cycle 8 (GC8). GC8 introduces significant changes, including predominantly reduced country allocations, reflecting a constrained global health financing environment and the need to prioritise limited resources in response to new global realities.

The International Network of People Who Use Drugs (INPUD) has consistently prioritised ensuring that communities of people who use drugs have access to timely, relevant information to enable meaningful engagement in Global Fund grant cycles. GC8 will be no exception, particularly given the shifting funding landscape and its implications for community-led responses.

INPUD will host a webinar titled “What You Need to Know About GC8”, aimed at supporting communities of people who use drugs to understand the key changes in GC8, their implications, and how to engage effectively in the grant cycle. Participants will learn about key entry points within GC8, community lessons and perspectives from previous grant cycles, and practical ways communities can work with Country Coordinating Mechanisms (CCMs).

title: Global Health Budget Advocacy Webinar: Protecting Global Health Investments: Advocacy Strategies in a Changing Budget Landscape
description:
Across low- and middle- income countries, domestic health budgets remain the single largest and most sustainable source of funding for infectious disease programs, maternal and child health, nutrition, pandemic preparedness, and health systems strengthening. Yet in many countries, health spending still falls short of national commitments and population needs — making civil society-led budget advocacy essential to closing the gap. This urgency is compounded by a shifting global funding landscape.

This webinar will convene health budget advocates, CSO leaders, and policy practitioners to share strategies for engaging policymakers on domestic health financing, highlight concrete examples of successful budget advocacy in LMICs, and identify opportunities for coordinated action across countries.

title: Local Leadership, Global Partnerships: Together Against Malaria
host: Outreach Network for Gene Drive Research, Malaria No More, Impact Santé Afrique, KEMRI
description:
In recent years, progress in the fight against malaria has stalled. A “perfect storm” of challenges – including funding shortfalls and rising resistance to available interventions – are threatening to put millions more lives at risk and undo decades of hard-won gains. In the face of these converging threats, countries across the African region – which bears the highest malaria burden globally – are leading efforts to strengthen domestic financing and advance the fight to end malaria through local ownership and innovation. At the same time, sustaining and accelerating progress against malaria will require collective action and cross-sector collaboration to close funding gaps, deliver new tools, and foster resilient health systems.

For World Malaria Day, the Outreach Network for Gene Drive Research, in collaboration with Malaria No More, Impact Santé Afrique and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI), will convene leading experts and researchers from the malaria community to explore how local leadership, global partnerships, and cross sectoral collaborations can advance the fight to end malaria.

title: Integrating HIV and TB Innovations into GC8 : How Global Fund Grants Can Catalyze Scale Up of Lenacapavir and New TB Diagnostics
description:
GFAN has invited colleagues from the Global Fund Secretariat’s HIV and TB teams to share insights on how Global Fund grants can support the integration of new HIV and TB innovations in GC8. Whether funding requests have already been submitted or are still under development, there remain opportunities in the GC8 planning process to advance ambitious targets for the scale up of innovative tools for HIV prevention and TB testing.

This webinar will provide a space for civil society and community colleagues to give perspective on ongoing efforts and opportunities to influence the integration of lenacapavir and nPoC testing in current planning processes, to highlight their experiences in advocating for inclusion of innovations in past cycles, to share key messages and resources related to lenacapavir and nPoC TB testing, and to ask questions of colleagues from the Global Fund Secretariat.

Lenacapavir represents a transformative prevention tool in the fight against HIV, while the new Pluslife MiniDock is a breakthrough tool for making the first step of TB testing both far easier for patients and far cheaper for TB programs. WHO guidelines have recently recommended both tools and the Global Fund has emphasized the value added by both innovations in its guidance on priorities for GC8 planning. As with past innovations, the level of investment and models of service delivery will be key to the impact of these technologies, and the voices of civil society and communities will be key to advancing the ambition of CCM plans for scale up.

title: CEPI briefing for CSOs on Bundibugyo Response
host: The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI)
description:
Since the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, CEPI has moved rapidly. We are working with WHO, Africa CDC, Gavi, and national authorities to activate our global preparedness networks and accelerate the research needed to support an effective response.

With no licensed Bundibugyo virus vaccine and limited evidence of cross‑protection from existing filovirus vaccines, CEPI is seeking to close a critical gap in global outbreak preparedness. We have rapidly advanced a portfolio of vaccine candidates by securing agreements with Moderna, IAVI, and the University of Oxford/Serum Institute of India, and launched a Call for Proposals which aims to rapidly advance the most promising early‑stage vaccine candidates toward clinical trials as fast as possible.

title: Pre-AIDS 2026 CHANGE update webinar
description:
We will be joined by Tara Herrick, Associate Director of Market Intelligence for Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI).
Tara will provide a deep dive into CHAI's latest HIV Market Update Memo, which lays out a grave reality: 16 months into US funding cuts and award cancellations for global health programs, along with reduced Global Fund country allocations, data show HIV prevention and treatment programs are falling, with no sign of recovery (yet).

We will dive into the evidence and share what communities are doing in response. The AIDS 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro is approaching fast—government officials from around the world and leaders of global health initiatives will be in attendance. AIDS 2026 is an opportunity to challenge our leaders to address these prevention and treatment access crises. We will discuss those opportunities for action and share plans.

title: Du GC7 au GC8 : Comprendre, suivre et influencer les engagements de cofinancement pour la lutte contre le VIH, la Tuberculose et le Paludisme
host: Le Fonds Mondial, GFAN Africa, Impact Sante Afrique, CS4ME
description:
Votre gouvernement a-t-il honoré ses engagements de cofinancement du Cycle 7 de la subvention du Fonds mondial ?

Si NON, une partie de son allocation pour le Cycle 8 (2027-2029) pourrait être réduite ⚠️. C'est la règle : une dette de cofinancement non payée au GC7 s'ajoute aux exigences du GC8. Les pays sont actuellement en revue technique, et la société civile a encore une fenêtre pour agir !

title: Twenty Years Strong: Grandmothers' Leadership in the HIV Response
description:
Celebrate 20 years of international grandmothers solidarity and centre the needs of older women and caregivers in lead up to AIDS 2026

The HIV epidemic has changed dramatically in the 20 years since the 2006 International AIDS Conference in Toronto and the launch of the Grandmothers to Grandmothers Campaign. Yet grandmothers continue to play a vital role in their communities and families and in the HIV response. On the eve of the 2026 International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, join the Stephen Lewis Foundation as we look back at 20 years of international grandmothers solidarity and look forward to how the needs and priorities of older women and caregivers must shape the future of the HIV response.

title: Virtual Press Conference: Launch of the Human Cost of Policy Shifts: A World in Turmoil
description:
In early 2025, abrupt funding cuts from the U.S. triggered a major shock and widespread service disruptions across already underfunded harm reduction services and programmes for people who use drugs. One year on, these cuts, combined with punitive drug policies, have pushed people who use drugs into a full-blown emergency. This is no longer just a financial crisis – it is a political and human rights crisis that is costing lives and dismantling community-led services.

Join INPUD for the launch of The Human Cost of Policy Shifts: A World in Turmoil, a follow-up study to the 2025 report, The Human Cost of Policy Shifts: The Fallout of US Foreign Aid Cuts on Harm Reduction Programming and People who Use Drugs.

title: Webinar : Leveraging Global Fund Grant Cycle 8 for Women's, Children's and Adolescent Health
host: Hub d'Apprentissage régional Afrique francophone du Fonds mondial, Partenariat pour la santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile (PMNCH), UNFPA, The Global Fund, The Anglophone Africa Learning Hub
description:
The Global Fund’s Grant Cycle 8 (2026–2028) offers a pivotal opportunity to integrate sexual, reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health (SRMNCAH) priorities into HIV, TB, malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) investments.
Le 8e cycle de subventions (GC8) du Fonds mondial de lutte contre le sida, la tuberculose et le paludisme marque un tournant décisif pour la santé sexuelle, reproductive, maternelle, néonatale, infantile et adolescente (SRMNCAH). Avec une enveloppe de 10,78 milliards USD confirmée pour la période 2026–2028, les pays éligibles sont actuellement en phase d’élaboration de propositions.
